subject: english
chapter_title: Bholi: Sulekha's Journey from Simpleton to Teacher

concepts.title: Bholi, the Neglected Fourth Child
concepts.definition: Sulekha, called Bholi the simpleton, is the fourth child of Numberdar Ramlal; a fall in infancy damaged her brain, smallpox left her face pocked, and the family neglected her education and prospects.
concepts.key_idea: When a primary school opens for girls, her mother sends Bholi thinking it might chance her luck, while the sisters fear losing jewellery and clothes to school rules.
question_patterns: why is bholi's father worried about her
for what unusual reasons is bholi sent to school

why did ramlal's wife agree to send bholi to school

solution_steps.explain: A fall at ten months and smallpox at two left Bholi slow of speech and pock-marked.
Pretty sisters Radha and Mangla were married well; Bholi stayed a worry at home.
When the tehsildar urged girls' schooling, Bholi was sent since her parents felt she needed the luck more.

concepts.title: The First Day at School and the Kind Teacher
concepts.definition: Afraid at school, Bholi finds hope in a gentle teacher whose soothing voice makes her feel someone cares; asked to say her name, she stammers, yet the teacher encourages rather than mocks her.
concepts.key_idea: The teacher gives her a picture book and promises to make her the most learned in the village, planting the seed of confidence.
question_patterns: how did bholi feel on her first day at school
why did bholi's heart thump when she was called to speak
how did the teacher encourage bholi when she stammered
what promise did the teacher make to bholi
what gift did the teacher give bholi on the first day
why did bholi begin to like her school

solution_steps.explain: Bholi wept at being separated from her mother and hid behind her father.
The soft, soothing voice and gentle questions drew Bholi out of her fear.
The teacher vowed to make Bholi learned and confident, and Bholi began to hope.

concepts.title: Years of Study Transform Bholi
concepts.definition: Education works its slow miracle: Bholi learns to read, speak without stammering, and carry herself with confidence, so that years later she stands transformed in dress and speech before her family.
concepts.key_idea: The village marvels that the dumb cow of a girl has turned into a confident young woman, proof of the teacher's quiet work.
question_patterns: how did education change bholi over the years
how did bholi overcome her stammer
what surprised the villagers about bholi later
how did bholi's appearance and speech change
why did bholi remain in school while others left
what does bholi's transformation prove about education

solution_steps.explain: Bholi learned to read and write, and the teacher's patient drills cured her stammer.
She dressed cleanly and spoke clearly, winning the school's respect.
Even her family saw that the once-simple Bholi had become assured and learned.

concepts.title: The Rejected Groom and Bholi's Dignity
concepts.definition: When the aged, lame widower Bishamber demands five thousand rupees as dowry and then insults her pock-marked face at the wedding, Bholi throws the garland into the fire and rejects the marriage with firm, clear speech.
concepts.key_idea: Her father begs her to bend, but Bholi's self-respect has grown: she will marry only an equal who knows her worth.
question_patterns: why did bholi throw the wedding garland into the fire

solution_steps.explain: Bishamber, older with grown children, first demanded a dowry, then taunted her face at the garland.
Bholi swept the garland into the fire and spoke without a single stammer.
She declared she would marry a man who respected her, stunning the gathering.

concepts.title: Bholi's Vocation: Serving as a Teacher
concepts.definition: Bholi resolves to become a teacher at her old school and serve where she was once a frightened child, promising her astonished teacher that she will care for her parents and carry the school's work forward.
concepts.key_idea: The girl once called a simpleton finds her life's work in the classroom, completing the story's claim that education gives the weak both voice and purpose.
question_patterns: what vocation did bholi choose at the end of the story
why does bholi want to become a teacher
how does bholi plan to care for her parents
how does the teacher react to bholi's decision
what does bholi's choice say about the power of education
how does the story bholi end and what is its message

solution_steps.explain: Bholi says she will teach in the same school where she learnt her first lessons.
She credits her teacher's kindness and promises to serve her parents in their old age.
Education turns the despised child into a giver, the story's closing message.
